title: Can Your AI Analyst Keep a Secret? - Aaron Linsky, Bridgewater & Nikhil Benesch, turbopuffer
talk_summary: Bridgewater and turbopuffer describe building a permission-aware vector search layer over 100M private documents, where every document has distinct access controls. The core engineering lesson is that naive post-filtering or pre-filtering both fail at scale, and combining them via cluster-level permission indexes yields fast, high-recall results.

takeaways.what_they_do: They reject retrieving top-K then discarding unauthorized docs, because recall collapses when the user's accessible subset is sparse; instead they index permissions per vector cluster and skip inaccessible clusters before scanning.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you do post-filtering, you kind of spiral outwards, and then at some point you have to give up

takeaways.what_they_do: They precompute which vector clusters contain at least one document a given principal can see, then search only those clusters and scan sequentially inside them (~200 docs/cluster).
takeaways.evidence_quote: first we find all of the clusters that Aaron has access to ... and then we search the closest clusters

takeaways.what_they_do: Before adding system complexity they anchor on the simplest possible solution and compute whether it meets the latency target, only adding indexing when the math says the naive approach fails.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We never want to introduce complexity to Turbo Puffer that's not justified.
